title: one thing that bugs me
body: i like the app and that it's free to use, but i just do not like how   words/sentences are presented in note previews. it just looks rather...unprofessional? it's most notable when i write my recipes in bullet order. instead of subhighlighting the first word/s in the preview like what apple notes does, it tries to fit most of what i wrote instead without accounting for the bullet points. i know i can turn this off by setting the preview to small, but i like having my notes be visible :( i just don't want them to look so garbled. hopefully this can be fixed in the future!

title: Windows bug
body:
I’ve been using this app for over 3 years, I love it. It works just fine on Mac. Recently, I got a PC and I moved my workspace there. There is a webpage version of this app but it doesn’t sync right. I was writing on my PC yesterday for all night and I woke up today check the same file on my phone. BOOM, nothing is there, nothing got saved. And the worst part is, the website will auto sync to the phone no matter what. Which means it will erase whatever I wrote on the website and go back to the old version of the file on my phone. ISN’T THIS STUPID?

这个软件真的哪里都好，就是这个在windows上跟mac的sync会出问题。不会即时同步，总是会以mac的版本为准。导致在windows上写的东西存不下来，一刷新就消失。又因为这个丢了一次东西，web到底怎么回事。
developer_response:
Hello, and sorry for this issue. Bear Web is still in beta and can have some bugs. Please contact our customer support, and we'll try to assist as soon as possible.
https://bear.app/contact/

title: My Teddy BEAR!
body:
This app has so many features that allow you to organize info under appropriate headers, and sub-headers! Once you get the hang of it you’ll have a cleanly organized listing of your data. 
> You will likely find yourself resetting the hierarchy of data in order to keep it organized in the area(s) where it belongs — otherwise you’ll find data under the correct Headers but in several locations. 
🔅With patience & time you can organize it into a clean collection of your data.

title: LOVE this app
body: I’m a big notes guy, and used to always just use the Notes app from Apple, but one day I needed to just scribble a drawing to get my point across and couldn’t do it, found this app and the rest is history. Everything from the super clean interface, to the quick and efficient way to jot down notes and label them with hashtags to help  categorize things - it’s seamless and honestly, one of the quickest subscriptions ive ever paid for. I use it daily, if not hourly
i feel like all the other note taking apps are more for aesthetic but i like that this one is actually practical and everything isn’t locked behind a paywall

title: Just keeps getting better
body: Love Bear, love everything about it. And the recent addition of mermaid and workspace as tags just keep making it better. It truly is a dream app.

title: I love this app!!
body: I love this app!! I love the different themes available, I love the live updates for the time of an entry, & I love the pin to top feature. I use this app for notes, to save links & package tracking numbers. I would like to suggest each entry show the day of the week, & the time. I also would like to suggest entries be stored together by each different month. Thank you for this app!! I use this app every day.

title: I’ve never written a review but this deserved one
body: I’ve used every note app in the App Store and always end up back on my iPhone notes app…until now. It’s perfect. Visually refined. Clean. The typography is so refreshing. I believe it’s their font which is cool. Shows they care. One of the reasons the other apps frustrate me is they’re all too clunky. This one is as simple as Notes but has every possible features cleverly hidden. The way menus are built is so intuitive. Endless ways to easily organize without the clutter of endless folders. You can customize everything. I can’t believe I’m saying this but it makes me feel good using it. lol Incredible job by the developers. Please make other apps. This level of artistry in app design is desperately needed. The craziest part it’s $30 a YEAR! Immediately cancelled my Evernote subscription which was $12 a month and sucks compared to this app.

title: Everything is GONE.
body: I love this app. I have been using it for probably several years at this point. I have kept everything in my notes, and I happen to tap too fast getting into the app, thinking I’m getting a “leave a review” pop up; they asked to make storage on my device and EVERYTHING is deleted, not even in the trash can, I mean completely gone! I hope there is a way to get them back, I hadn’t made any backups 🥲

title: Good markdown viewer, not a fan of tags, expensive subscription
body: I’m looking for a new Notes app. I like the color themes that Bear offers. The app looks really good too. The text and paragraph formatting options are limited though. Bear is good as a markdown viewer. What I don’t like, however: 1) in order to create folders and nested folders, I have to use tags 2) I was also very turned off by the subscription.. $30 a year? I’d like to see a  reasonable one-time pay, or reasonable yearly subscription price. $30 a year is patently absurd if you’re not a heavy user and only just using the app as a markdown viewer.
developer_response: We understand your preference for folders, but Bear was built around the concept of tagging from the very beginning, and, after 10 years, we are still convinced that mixing its tags system with folders is not the right choice.

title: Clunky messy ui
body: Sure it looks "clean" at first but it automatically adds markups that show every time you try to edit a word. So if you delete part of it you end up with bunch of asterisks to delete. That's not clean. Would prefer no markups at all. And having to pull up a secondary keyboard for every formatting task gets tiresome and kills work flow. Why not a long press menu for frequent formatting functions? And can't select more than one cell in tables. Honestly would rather go back to apple notes if wasn't so slow on my older device.

title: Great app at a great price
body: I love the Bear app. It’s WAY better than Evernote and reasonably priced. Keep up the great work!

title: I’m using this nonstop now
body: I love this notes app is just what I needed! Though I’m giving this 4 stars because I really wish the lock notes feature would be free.

title: Sadly, voiceover support is lacking.
body: I was really excited to try this app especially since so many people love it and because I’m looking for something that is simple that also supports wiki linking. unfortunately, as a VoiceOver user, I’m finding the app very difficult to use. Many of the buttons are not labeled and also voiceover has trouble tracking focus as I move around the app. As such, the app is currently not usable for me at least on iOS. I hope that the developers will consider adding more robust voiceover support in the future, I would definitely be a very happy user..

title: Exactly what I needed
body: I was looking for an Evernote alternative where I could use tags, and this is perfect. I both like to write and store recipes using tags for season, type, occasion etc. The support for nested tags is much appreciated, and their Pro plan is very reasonable. Not much is paywalled (it’s just cloud features, themes, and search), so give it a try!

title: Almost
body:
It’s almost perfect, it won’t render math or PDFs or anything, it was working, the update broke it

I love how it looks but the exporting and rendering are pretty fundamental and I feel like it should really be able to do more, like why not also have rich text as an option and if it’s only markdown then it’s a pretty high priority that it should do markdown literally flawlessly and it doesn’t 

Hope it gets fixed asap 
If still recommend it but with warnings and if there were anything else better this app could easily lose to that 

There are so few options for anything like this it’s pretty mind blowing

title: Extremely suspect privacy policy
body: Expressly states data can be used for beta testing and worst of all the testing is done with what is quite arguably the least privacy conscious company of the 21st century: Microsoft. Not to be outdone, the rest of the policy is extremely vague but lends itself to the interpretation that absent written notice provided to either the developer or applicable authorities OR both (language isn’t clear and would need to dive deeper), you have absolutely no it rly zero expectation of privacy here. In a market with 50 other competitors, this isn’t the way to do business IMO. Massive wasted opportunity here
developer_response:
The App Center beta testing data collection was incorrectly reported in our terms of services and it's no longer used. Since 2023, we have been using TestFlight to ship and test betas of Bear. Thanks for reporting this issue.

Regarding the privacy and security provided by Bear, you can find more information in the link below, but in short, we can't access your notes, and we don't collect data other than what the App Store provides or crashlogs not reporting using information.
https://bear.app/faq/syncing-privacy/

title: Just better than anything comparable
body:
- It works
- It works consistently 
- Great UI
- Smooth down to the smallest of interactions 
- Fast
- Same great experience on every Apple device 

No matter how many times I try other note taking apps, none of them come close to the simple, great experience of Bear.

title: Should need no introduction
body: Bear slaps. I've used it for like 8 years now. Super simple, just the right amount of complexity. Themes and styles are beautiful, including all the custom icons. Sync is always super fast and smooth. Exporting, tagging, formatting, all just work exactly how you'd want. Everything feels crisp and easy to use, especially and most importantly the note editor UI, which is truly perfect. Keep doing what you're doing dev team give somebody a raise

title: ipad rendering bugged for months now
body: when using bear on the ipad in windowed mode (not full screen), sometimes following a link within a note causes a bug with rendering where the bottom portion of the note is not rendered. you can sometimes fix it by restarting bear.
developer_response: Sorry for this issue. Do you mind contacting our customer support so we can ask you more about the problem you are experiencing? https://bear.app/contact/

title: The very best! ♡
body: This app is reliable, easy to navigate, and stylish. I love using it every day! Please consider adding a feature for user-made themes in the future! And a feature to toggle a note’s history + restore versions!

title: Bear is the Best!
body:
Hands down my favorite notes app I’ve ever used. It’s getting more features all the time and has everything I need. Most aesthetically pleasing app, too.

I love how it syncs across my iPad and MacBook, and the way it centers the content inside the window is an amazing but simple feature that not all other notes apps have.

Well worth the money. My go-to for many years now. Small development team I believe, too, so I’m more than happy supporting this gem.

title: Great for saving info
body: Well, it was a great app, but the latest update just screwed up the copy and paste function.  Used to be you could just copy and paste, then edit your data; now after you copy, it gives you a multiple choice for paste for which no selected options work, so they just rendered my favorite note taking app useless for copying data to edit.
developer_response:
Hello,
I'm not sure what you are referring to here, but we have not introduced or changed how copy and paste work in Bear. If you care about telling us more about the problem you are experiencing, please write to our customer support team.
https://bear.app/contact/

title: Fantastic
body: Love it. It’s a little glitchy sometimes but overall I love the design and feel

title: Almost Perfect Out of the Box
body:
I would give it 5 stars if there was the ability to disable word wrap in code blocks and allow a sideways scroll. I do a lot of code snippets, but most lines are beyond the iPhone Pro Max screen width. Callouts could benefit from this as well.

It would also be great if we could add or edit a CSS stylesheet file for the HTML export, or dare I ask for in-app style customizations beyond the prebuilt theme and the font face and size/spacing options (which are great by the way, thank you!)

Finally, but not an issue of this app at all and not affecting its rating, would the developers PLEASE, PRETTY PLEASE make a Windows app, or at least a web app I could use on Windows? Then I would be a diehard forever customer.

title: Thank you for the safe space
body: This app feels safe, calm, useful, simple.

title: I want to love it so badly
body:
Bear would be my perfect notes app, and I would gladly pay the subscription for it. 

However, the keyboard toolbar/text editor on iPhone is so bad, especially when compared with the default Apple notes. (Please just copy how Apple notes sets up their keyboard toolbar, it’s so much better).

If you want to format anything, it is such a headache and so incredibly slow because everything is hidden behind a formatting menu icon, which you have to press, select the formatting option you want, then change back to keyboard. This could very easily just be one button press like it is in Apple Notes. And considering how often I format notes, this time adds up quickly. Aesthetic at the cost of efficiency is useless. 

Also pls pls pls just copy the way Apple’s todo lists work. I want to be able to drag around todo list items. 

Unfortunately, Bear is an app clearly designed to be used with a mouse and keyboard, not fingers and touchscreens. I think it is so beautiful, and I love the organizational structure with the tags and markdown. But this basic functionality that is missing is so core to a notes app that I will very sadly have to replace it with Apple notes. 

If they fix this, I’m buying the subscription and changing my review to 5 stars.

title: What I’ve been looking for
body: It’s like it was made for me

title: All my work is gone
body: They updated the app and absolutely everything that I’ve kept there is gone and customer service has helped very very little. If ur gonna use the app at least keep your work backed up elsewhere

title: Indispensable
body: I do a ton of notetaking, and Bear is now my indispensable tool for doing so. The UX is great across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, syncing across devices just works with iCloud without any extra subscription, and the Markdown support is great for portability between systems like blogs.

title: Brilliant, lovely
body:
So easy to use and intuitive. 

The aesthetics make it fun. I haven’t found a better app for organizing all the notes, documents, links, and courses I collect and refer to to support my career-change coaching practice. 

The tagging system allows me to classify something by topic and also author or source. It’s a beautiful personal library. 

And the customer service is extremely responsive.

title: Clean and Powerful
body:
This app shines in the little details: it’s crazy fast, compare it to Apple notes and you will see a night and day difference, especially for long notes. It has table of contents, which makes it easy to navigate long notes. The tag system is miles better than folders. You can manage your todos by following a thin line under each of your notes that shows the progress of your todos in the note. It supports latex! So you can write math formulas now. It has web access. It has a nice menu of themes. It shows you unmentioned backlinks: you can reference other notes that mention the title of your current note. You can lock notes with attachments. You can copy links to each note. You can export to multiple formats. You can draw (although here it’s a bit basic) and have Bear detect words in your images. It gives you useful stats about your notes. And I could keep going.

You would not tell half of these when you first open the app, and that’s the point. Its power is modest. It enables you and gets out of the way so you can work. Their dev team is small and slow, but they deliver. Late sometimes, but they deliver. This app is a powerhouse.

title: Tried them all-came home to Bear
body:
This app is so streamlined that it can be deceptive how brilliant it is. Bear works with your mind—without friction. 

Hashtags are one of five key power tools here. Use them to create a filing system, as well as to cross index any files you want.

Bear seems simple, but it is in fact the most elegant writing tool out there. In its elegant simplicity exists ultimate creative power.

As a fiction writer, with many large projects on my plate, I can tell you—as someone who has tried all the excellent writing apps out there—nothing comes close to Bear.

It’s exactly what it needs to be, leaves everything else in its wake, is created by people who design with pure intent, which is why it’s literally pristine.

Even if you doubt, master its incredibly simple tools, and build out a file system using the tags— they nest like breadcrumb trails…and there you go. You no longer have to choose a folder, or even a title. Just write, just flow, just go.

title: Perfect & Private
body: I’ve had this for years and love it. Just open and start writing, and the company does NOT extract or use any of your information, location, contacts, etc., which is a great sign of integrity, especially today.

title: almost good
body: if you could send notes to people like in evernote i would drop other note apps and go full bear. upgrade it and grab the money on the table bear

title: Voiceover users beware
body: I didn't even get to read  the welcome notes before deleting this app. The side menu will not stop popping out, no matter what I do. The advice was to swipe right from the middle of the screen to avoid this but nothing worked. And if the welcome notes have titles, VO didn't read them. Just skip this one. Save yourself the headache.

title: Clean interface, intuitive function
body: I’ve tried pretty much every web clipping app out there in pursuit of the perfect system to store and organize my research. Bear comes pretty close! The UI is simple and uncluttered (super important to me as someone with difficulties navigating busy designs). The nesting note system keeps all my notes and clippings well organized and easily searchable. Unlike other Markdown-based apps I tried, there was no learning curve—use was completely intuitive, so I could get to work right away. I particularly like the note menu design with its ability to assign an icon to each category—again, as someone who has difficulty navigating dense text designs, the icons provide a helpful identifier to help me quickly navigate to my most-used categories.

title: Solid and beautiful text editor
body: I’ve used Bear for a few years now. I really enjoy the functionality, UI, and ease of formatting. I have the yearly subscription, so my notes sync across devices readily. I can also adjust font, spacing, and color themes easily. I’m not an advanced Markdown user, but I’m beginning to learn more features I’ve barely touched, like making your notes into your own pseudo-wiki (!). It’s really nice.

title: Excellent for so many things
body: I’ve been using Bear Notes almost from the beginning. It was slow going at first and I hung in there as Bear moved closer and closer to 2.0 and I have to tell you after using nearly all of the options that are out there for note taking, journaling and more, there’s no better.  So if you’re stuck with another note app, and want to see what else is out there, give Bear a try. You will not regret it. Excellent work developers, I look forward to being with you for years to come.

title: One of a kind!
body: Beautiful, efficient, and versatile! This is a one-of-a-kind app that I’ve made an inextricable part of my daily flow. Truly, it’s a masterpiece of elegance in software design. My only hope is the devs keep focus, as its versatility is going to encourage adamant recommendations for all kinds of added functionality and integration that could easily pull the app in a thousand different directions. I include myself among the masses. I wish the devs would add integration with the native iOS apps, especially the calendar and reminders.

title: Amo
body: Me gusta mucho,tiene muchas opciones de texto,puedes hacer de todo un poco,es buena para ipad y teléfonos,simplemente me encanta

title: 不好用
body: 非常垃圾。辛苦写了几个小时的字全没了。不建议使用。

title: The best writing app.
body: My only go to app for writing. I love it.

title: Lovely, but a few suggestions!
body:
I’ve been using Bear for years, long before Bear 2 released and it truly has come a long way! As a student, I don’t use Bear for anything particularly professional. I’m just a person who enjoys keeping everything simple and organized. Bear is just that. It’s easy to use yet has always been steps ahead of the iOS Notes app as far as features and UI go. I use other apps for structure and organization like Obsidian, but everything I do starts in Bear. If I need to write anything at all, I open Bear without feeling overwhelmed by assigning it a category immediately. 
I’m a Bear Pro user and I don’t plan on letting go of Bear anytime soon so
here are a few tiny things I’d love to see in the future: 
1. There are a few instances where I like to be able to have a note throughout all of a tag’s subtags and main page out of convenience. For example, if I have a note called “resources” with the tags #physics/GR and #physics, currently the tag will only appear in the GR subtag. 
2. I wish the pencil icon next to external links could be disabled. 
3. It would be nice if users could adjust the primary action that appears in the menu. For example, the current first attachment action is Take Photo and any other requires you to hold down the button. I personally use the Add Images option way more so it would be more convenient if users could decide what shortcut appears on top.

title: Just a few annoyances
body: Bear is one of my favorite note-taking apps. It’s beautifully designed and incredibly intuitive to use. I just wish it had an archive option — sometimes I want to hide older notes without deleting them or cluttering my daily tags. Also, the Trash folder is always visible at the top of my tags, which can be a bit distracting. It would be nicer if it were hidden or moved to the bottom. Overall, it’s an amazing app with just a couple of small things that could make it perfect.

title: Best Notes App
body: I’ve tried multiple brand name note taking apps and this is by far my favorite. Sleek, simple and has all the features I need.

Need to consolidate between apps and shifted to Obsidian but that’s for a personal decision across platforms and also for higher expressions of note taking that Bear doesn’t have.  One key plus is pasting  images into the note, much easier than with Obsidian. But Bear has been a great mobile app.

title: very functional without extra junk
body: I replaced evernote with bear about 9 months ago and wish I had done it 2 years ago. Bear is super functional, I get pretty much everything I need. Get bear pro, it is completely worth it and the best deal of all the notes apps.

title: Used to like this more
body: There’s been a UI revision in the last while that’s made it super confusing to do things like add images to notes from my phone (go to BIU, open a keyboard, hold down on a camera icon, etc). It’s not at all fluid.

title: My go-to writing app
body: I downloaded Bear back in 2016 and it’s been my exclusive writing app since. The interface is intuitive yet non-intrusive, something very important to me. I can write without a bunch of buttons scattered across the screen and can pull them up easily when I do need them. The tag system is amazing and easy to work with and I love the small touches like changing tag icons! I write every day and it’s thanks to Bear!

title: Great Note app for light formatting
body: I don’t like the iOS Notes app much.  I wanted a text editor with light formatting options, like WordPad in Windows.  Bear is perfect for this.  You can apply bold, italic, underline, strike-through or highlight to text, have bullet lists, numbered lists, H1, H2, H3.  You can add footnotes.  It’s got pretty much everything I need.  Hashtags make organization easy.  These features are available with the free app, no subscription necessary.

title: Honest review
body:
This app has nice features, but it doesn’t beat Apple Notes, which is free.
For specific needs, I already use Microsoft Word and Apple Pages.
So I’ve got more than enough apps that cover everything Bear does, and more.

The only edge is exporting to multiple formats, but copy and paste to Word or Pages does the job.
Paying $30/year ($2.5/month) makes no sense with all the overlap.
Subscriptions add up, and apps like Procreate or Inshot, for example, in their industry give much more for less money.

I’d only consider paying for Bear with a one-time lifetime license price, or a much cheaper plan, where many more people wouldn’t mind paying for, something like $10/year.

For the features and design alone I would give 5 stars.

But the pricing is overselling and overwhelming and the world full of subscriptions.

If you decide to change your pricing plan, to something that makes more sense from a consumer standpoint, please let me know.

title: This is such a good application!
body: I’ve been a Bear user for many years.  It’s very easy to use, making even complex sets of notes easy to create and manage.  Bear puts the polish on notes like no other.  The developers are actively adding new features, and updates are meaningful and useful.  There are several very good notes apps out there, but Bear is excellent and elegant.  Like your iPhone, Mac, or iPad, everything just works and works well.

title: Good, but files sometimes disappear.
body: I have been using this note app to copy and organize my old recipes.  It is easy enough to use, once one learns the special characters needed for anything outside of plain script.  My problem is that notes occasionally are erased, through no keystroke I can find.  If I try to correct a spelling, the note disappears, completely erased.  It is not shown on the list, a search for key words finds nothing, and categories no longer show the note.  Some of these are old family recipes, and if I have deleted the source copy, it is completely lost.  This app is SO CLOSE to being exactly what I need, but how can I trust an app that saves “most” of the notes, but randomly drops others?  If I need to keep an old copy, just to be safe, why would I need this one for a duplicate?

title: Almost perfect
body: Great note app does most things iOS notes can do and maybe more  except make folders and sub folders to organize notes . And add audio files . If you could add these features I would say price is justified .

title: App is stutters and very buggy after mathjax update
body: This is a great app normally, but I hope the mathjax feature gets more polished soon, or please just revert this app back to previous version until the feature is more ready.  As it is, the app is almost unusable for me.

title: Best App I have on my phone
body: I love this app!! It’s so useful and a lot better than the regular notes app. Definitely recommend

title: Just wonderful
body:
Like many other people, I have used practically every Notes app on the planet trying to find “the one“. Bear is “the one”.

I think the biggest advantage Bear has is its broad feature set is grounded in focused simplicity. No app can be all things to all people and still be usable, so the developers have had to say “no” a lot.

Making the vastly improved text editor is going to help Bear remain viable for a long time. I read in their Discourse community that they test the text editor with the entire Bible as a single note!

The next big difference is going to be the upcoming web app.

title: Cute Idea
body:
When I was looking for a notes app, the name and icon to this felt cute, so I checked it out. I like the simplicity and childlike feel to it. It has the features you would expect. A three columned layout, ability to create tags, ability to attach files, and plenty of text formatting options.

One thing that I wasn’t a fan of is how to create tags. You have to create a hashtag symbol in your note, rather than to just create a new tag in the folder list. Some tags may need to be repeated several times, and so I would rather create a new note from a folder that automatically assigns the tags.

Aside from that, this is a cute little app, and I do recommend it.
developer_response: Hello, I can understand your preferences. However, we provide tag autocomplete to minimise the friction, and creating a new note inside a tag automatically provides the tag in the new note.

title: New callouts are gamechanging… but
body:
Callouts are exactly what Bear needed; they resolve the longstanding workaround of using quote blocks. I can comfortably say that with callouts there are no other notetaking apps that accomplish Bear’s balance of utility and simplicity

That said I do have some constructive feedback:

1. Spacing below callouts is awkward. Text/lists are either directly under the callout (as in touching the bottom edge) or have an additional line break that makes the following content seem unrelated.

2. A neutral callout background would be useful. The various colors are well-designed, but sometimes I find myself wanting the spatial separation without the added emphasis

3. The option to use emojis as the icon could be useful. I appreciate the thoughtfulness behind the callout types, as it makes using them much less cumbersome, however having the option to replace the icon would make the callouts more versatile and personal

Thanks for great update!

title: Best Note Taking App
body: This might be my first review on the App Store. This is a fantastic app. I’ve used Onenote, Notion, Obsidian, and many others and keep coming back to bear for one reason. Simplicity. It can be as complex or as simple as you want, but the simplicity it creates for the user is just so good. It syncs with iCloud securely, and attachments are search with their super fast search. Highly recommend.

title: Sync Issues
body: I’m a big fan of this app, but over the last few years there’s been sync issues, where my laptop and phone app disconnect and I’m not able to catch the disconnect/have to troubleshoot months later. The app also closes if I scroll too fast/far down the list.

Sorry for the issue you experienced. Please contact our customer support if you haven't already. We'll address your sync issues as soon as possible.

title: DELETE NOTES RIGHT NOW!
body:
My original review trashed this app so badly—heck, I even called out the Apple editor!—that, looking back on it, I wonder what was wrong with me that day I reviewed it.

     Even without a subscription, there is so much you can do with this app. Has anyone ever complimented how great your Notes note looked? No, because Notes doesn't let you change its font, or let you add footnotes, or have half a dozen "heading" styles, or have anything else to make the note nice to look at. Bear has all I mentioned and more. 

   As the current subtitle suggests, Bear has Markdown, the thing that lets you format with punctuation. You know—italics with asterisks, boldface with double asterisks, highlighting with double equal signs. If that sounds unappealing, there's an extra keyboard that lets you do all this without typing lots of random punctuation marks. 

  This app has all that Notes has and so, so much more. I can only find two big issues: syncing and tags.

   Syncing between devices is a locked feature. Not every feature can be free, sure, but I'm not paying just to have the same notes in both places. It's not exactly a problem for me, but if you NEED to sync, it will be for you.

  The tag problem, however, is a problem every user has to deal with. Instead of folders, notes in Bear are organized solely by tags, created by doing #this. It's nice that notes that fit in multiple categories can have multiple tags, but this system is clunky, ugly, 
and—forgive me, please—kind of stupid. Even after all the complaints other reviewers have made (not to mention my own first review), the developers absolutely refuse to change this. You've seen the responses!

   Despite its problems, Bear is the best notes app I know of. I deleted Notes a long time ago.
developer_response:
> why waste time adding all the "#lalaloopsey" nonsense when you could have created the note within the file it needs to go in?

Because you can do it without leaving the keyboard you are writing in. This functionality is also available in Apple Notes.

> I do not need that or exportation

You don't need it but this is currently another huge difference with Apple Notes. Notes is currently a closed system and it's very complex to move or export your work from it. We worked hard to adopt an open format people can easily move from or export for different purposes.

>  In conclusion, Bear looks better than Notes, but looking better is Bear's sole advantage. Be real, Apple editor: It is no better than yours.

Nah, it's way better :)

title: Nice UI, horrible UX
body:

During my evaluation on an iPad, I found the process of attaching photos to a note to be particularly frustrating. The method for adding images from the photo library is far from intuitive—I had to resort to searching google for instructions, which reflects a serious shortcoming in the app’s user experience.

I previously used Bear regularly a couple of years ago and recently decided to revisit it. Unfortunately, it falls short when compared to Apple Notes, both in terms of usability and overall value. The interface feels unnecessarily complicated, and its lack of intuitiveness is a major barrier to productivity. While the app performs well for basic note-taking, any attempt to go beyond that requires external help, which should not be the case in a well-designed product.

There is clear potential here, but the current user experience leaves much to be desired. I strongly recommend investing in more thorough UX research and usability testing to better align the interface with users’ expectations and workflows.

title: Quality App Uses Atypical Organization
body:
Bear is a nicely designed app that uses an unusual tagging structure for file organization. I think it will work well for many users looking for an Apple Notes replacement that uses plain text however, certain design decisions make it unusable for me. 

Bear doesn’t use a traditional hierarchy of directories for note organization but instead uses a tagging system that includes the option for nesting. Unfortunately, Bear doesn’t offer the ability to filter on multiple tags at once, which is to say constructing a query as simple as “tag1 AND tag2 AND tag3” can’t be handled in the UI without writing a string query. That’s a dealbreaker for me. 

It’s not exactly fair to judge Bear on this, but the general community opinion of the feature I’m describing seems to be negative, so I don’t expect it to be added.
developer_response: Yes... It's not fair :)

title: Not worth the coin.  You have to pay to store to iCloud?!
body:
You have to pay to store to iCloud?!  That’s silly and greedy.

I have been developing software for over 40 years.  I can understand wanting to get paid for your work.  But this limitation makes this software untestable for one’s environment.  Free apps do save to iCloud.

It also doesn’t allow you to edit the raw .md files, which free apps do as well.

So where is the value add if you pay for it?  None.
developer_response:
Bear uses CloudKit and a local database. Both are design choices allowing us to design how sync works and the functionalities we want, the way we want. We stand by this choice because it allowed us to keep this independent project alive for over 8 years with hundreds of competing apps financed by VCs.

If you want to test sync and all the pro functionalities, you can activate the subscription for 2 weeks. If you want to use free apps or any other app, I suggest not complaining about business model choices you don't understand.

title: Not “in-app” purchase. SUBSCRIPTION based!
body:
EDIT 04/16/25: Annual price raised to $29.99. Same complaints as before. Software is not a service and I will not RENT it from you. 
——
Previous review:

I am sick and tired of all these apps that claim to be free with “in-app purchases” that you think will be a reasonable $3 or $5 price tag for something simple like the basic ability to sync your writing across two devices (something Google notes does for FREE) only to discover after you’ve installed it that it’s SUBSCRIPTION based and will charge you $20 a year for something that should be a standard feature in a writing application! 

No, I will not subscribe. I will leave you negative feedback, delete the app, and avoid your company in the future until you catch on that users are NOT interested in paying multiple times for software. I’d have BOUGHT THIS APP OUTRIGHT if your prices were reasonable, but a $20 annual fee is absurd. After two years your app will cost TWICE what Scrivener does and have fewer features! 

Uninstalled and a complaint has been filed with the Apple Store that they stop showing subscription apps as “in-app purchases” and start showing them as “subscription-based fees” so I know not to waste my time downloading them.

PS: Scrivener, which has about twenty times the features of this app, is a one time fee of $25. Less if you get it during National Novel Writing Month. I bought that software without complaint on two platforms at full price because they were UP FRONT and HONEST about their pricing structure and it is WORTH it.

title: WARNING FOR TRANSFERRING NOTES
body: Let me start off by saying I love bear and have been using it for maybe half a decade now. I have tons of notes in there, and even with the free version it does exactly what I need it to do. So then here comes the issue: I recently got a new iPad and wanted to copy the notes from my old iPad onto the new one (I have the app on all my devices, but because I have the free version, I just copy and transfer whatever I need to). I hadn’t had the chance to do that until today, so I had time to start new notes on this new device (including notes I take for my classes). I was under the assumption that restoring a backup would import all of the files that I saved a backup of on my old device. There was NO WARNING that my current notes would be deleted if I restored this data. I did not have a backup of the notes in my new device either. Again, this is a great app, but I can’t forgive the lack of warning that caused me to lose all those incredibly important notes, even if in hindsight “restoring” data implies overwriting it. Even your average video game does this kind of warning. To the developers, please add clearer warnings and descriptions for what restoring a backup entails WITHIN THE APP, rather than just on your website. And to other app users, don’t be stupid like me and accidentally overwrite all your local files!

body: I saw a few people extolling this app. I downloaded it, but it doesn’t even open an existing not. I tap and tap nothing then randomly it might open. I only used for two minutes! Glad I didn’t waste a lot of time on this app. Uninstalled - back to the search!

title: Simple, Sleek
body: One of the best app to write notes that crave simplicity. The app is sleek, simple having limited but best in class features required to manage and organized notes. Loved the fact that it’s not overloaded with features and kept simple. Thank you team !!

title: Looks like a 5 Star Wiki page when I write 😍
body: First of all I love how most of the tools are free and this has really helped me in school. Before my notes looked sloppy but now they look great. What’s also helped me is that I know HTML Scripting so I know the pros and cons of the code. Also knowing the type of code has helped me learn the buttons A lot. Overall best note taking app. I use this daily and sometimes for fun so I don’t remember facts. I wish this app gets More People using it so the Creators can get more money because their work is the Best . 10/10 Thank you Devs for making this app. And always Remember, Never stop asking questions. Bye guys! ✌️

title: It’s ok, from the developers’ responses, they’re pretty opinionated on it not getting better.
body: I tried Bear several years ago and it didn’t work for me mainly because I have an Android phone, and need it to sync with my phone, not just Apple devices (MacBook and iPad Pro). I looked into it again thinking maybe I could use it for some more work that I’ll just not do on my phone. I like tagging systems for some things. They’re good. But Folders are also good, and there is room for both. Bear seems to think only tags are good, and folders are bad. Both would be better. But instead, Bear responds to requests for folders with Nah, we like it this way, and with some extra snark on the side. Ok, do your thing. You lost me as a customer with that one though.

title: Powerful simplicity
body: I am a huge fan of this app. It does exactly what it needs to do, and in a very powerful way, without bloat or distraction. It’s one of those systems that allows complexity through a very simple set of rules. Take a day or two to use it and I think you’ll be impressed.
